paragraphs: Neural networks contain nonsmooth operations such as ReLU and quantization, so nearby gradients can point in conflicting directions. The paper identifies resulting gradient oscillation as a weakness of adaptive optimizers. Singularity-aware Adam responds to local geometric instability instead of treating every region as smoothly varying.

A Local Geometric Instability metric estimates the diameter of the Clarke subdifferential using the variance of randomized directional derivatives. Exponential damping reduces step sizes in unstable regions while allowing faster updates in smooth ones. Differential-inclusion analysis gives almost-sure convergence to approximate Clarke stationary points at an O(1/√T) rate.

Tests on quantization-aware training and noisy small-batch learning outperform AdamW and Prox-SGD, with accuracy gains reaching 4.54% on CIFAR-100 and 4.27% on TinyImageNet. The contribution connects a measurable form of local nonsmoothness to an adaptive optimization rule, making the response to oscillation depend on geometry rather than only gradient magnitude.
icml-2026-singularity-aware-optimization.tldr: Singularity-aware Adam measures local gradient instability and damps updates to improve nonsmooth and noisy training.

paragraphs: Simulating cloth and other soft objects requires modeling deformation together with environmental forces and robot actions. A simulator that ignores control or relies on an unsuitable fixed physical model can become unstable over long interactions. SoMA learns those coupled effects in a neural real-to-simulation framework.

The model represents the scene with learned 3D Gaussian splats and combines deformable dynamics, environmental influences, and robot joint actions in a shared latent space. Training is end to end and does not require a predefined physical model. This makes robot-conditioned interaction part of the dynamics representation itself.

On real-world manipulation data, SoMA reports a 20% improvement in resimulation accuracy and generalization. It also supports stable long-horizon tasks such as cloth folding beyond observed trajectories. The significance is a controllable learned simulator for interactions that are difficult to specify analytically, with demonstrated stability over extended manipulation rather than only short visual reconstruction.
icml-2026-soma-a-real-to-sim-neural-simu.tldr: SoMA jointly models soft-object dynamics and robot actions with Gaussian splats for stable, generalizable real-to-sim manipulation.

paragraphs: Multi-turn reinforcement learning can collapse when agents keep producing actions that neither resolve uncertainty nor advance a task. Better reward assignment alone may not prevent that wasted exploration. T²PO explicitly monitors exploration at both the token and interaction levels to make training more stable.

At the token level, the method intervenes in thinking when the marginal change in uncertainty falls below a threshold. At the turn level, it detects interactions with negligible exploratory progress and resamples them. These controls aim to redirect computation while a rollout is being constructed rather than merely discard poor trajectories afterward.

Evaluations on WebShop, ALFWorld, and Search QA show improved stability, exploration efficiency, and task performance. The contribution is a fine-grained mechanism for recognizing when additional generation has stopped being informative. It connects training reliability to the quality of exploratory actions, extending the stabilization problem beyond how rewards are assigned to completed trajectories.
icml-2026-t-2-po-uncertainty-guided-expl.tldr: T²PO uses token- and turn-level uncertainty signals to redirect uninformative exploration and stabilize multi-turn agent training.

paragraphs: Bayesian analysis usually requires specifying a prior and likelihood, which can be difficult when a powerful predictive model is already available. Martingale posteriors offer another route: use a predictive rule to obtain uncertainty about a quantity defined through a loss. TabMGP applies that idea to TabPFN for tabular data.

The target scientific parameter need not be a parameter of TabPFN’s implicit model. Instead, the martingale-posterior construction uses its predictions to recover a distribution for the estimand of interest. This separates the choice of a useful predictive engine from the choice of the scientific quantity whose uncertainty matters.

The resulting credible sets have near-nominal coverage and often outperform handcrafted martingale-posterior constructions and standard Bayesian baselines. The contribution makes a tabular foundation model usable for inferential tasks beyond point prediction, while evaluating whether its uncertainty sets have the intended empirical coverage rather than assuming predictive accuracy automatically supplies calibrated inference.
icml-2026-tabmgp-martingale-posterior-wi.tldr: TabMGP turns TabPFN’s predictive rule into posterior uncertainty for scientific estimands, with near-nominal reported coverage.

paragraphs: Spoken dialogue can benefit from preparing a response while the other person is still talking. Conventional explicit reasoning often begins afterward, adding delay. FLAIR develops a latent-reasoning mechanism that operates concurrently with speech perception in a full-duplex dialogue model.

During listening, the model recursively feeds its previous latent embedding into the next step. This maintains a continuous internal computation while respecting the causal order of incoming speech. An evidence-lower-bound objective supports supervised fine-tuning with teacher forcing, avoiding a requirement for annotated reasoning traces.

Experiments achieve competitive speech-benchmark results and strong performance on full-duplex interaction measures. The contribution is a training and architecture design that integrates response preparation into the listening period without adding a separate post-listening reasoning stage. Its value lies in matching computation to conversational timing while maintaining the quality and flexibility needed for interactive speech.
icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.tldr: FLAIR performs causal latent reasoning while listening, supporting responsive full-duplex speech without explicit reasoning annotations.

paragraphs: Adding 3D features to a multimodal language model does not guarantee that it uses the right geometry for a question. Indiscriminate fusion can introduce redundancy or misalign spatial and semantic information. GeoThinker lets the model retrieve geometric evidence according to its current reasoning needs.

Spatial-Grounded Fusion is inserted at selected layers, where visual-semantic representations query task-relevant geometry through frame-specific cross-attention. Importance Gating further emphasizes structures useful within each frame. This changes geometry integration from a global feature stream into a selective information-gathering operation.

The method reaches a peak score of 72.6 on VSI-Bench and generalizes to settings including embodied referring and autonomous driving. The contribution is an active fusion mechanism backed by spatial-task evaluations. The results suggest that access to geometric information is only part of the problem: the model also needs a way to choose and use that information at the appropriate reasoning stage.
icml-2026-thinking-with-geometry-active-.tldr: GeoThinker selectively retrieves task-relevant geometry inside a multimodal model, improving spatial reasoning and downstream generalization.

paragraphs: Federated adversarial learning combines distributed training with robustness to perturbed inputs. Existing theory has emphasized whether optimization converges, leaving less understanding of performance on unseen data. This paper uses algorithmic stability to study generalization across a broad family of such methods.

For SGD-based algorithms, the authors derive bounds that depend on adversarial perturbation strength, showing how stronger attacks can worsen the generalization guarantee. They then use Moreau-envelope optimization to obtain a perturbation-independent bound. This provides a theoretically motivated way to manage robustness and generalization together.

The analysis extends to black-box settings through zeroth-order optimization, where clients need not expose local gradients. The contribution is a unified generalization perspective that spans ordinary gradient access and a more restricted practical setting. It clarifies why convergence or resistance to stronger training attacks alone does not fully characterize the quality of a federated adversarial learner.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.tldr: Stability analysis explains perturbation-dependent generalization in federated adversarial learning and motivates smoother, black-box-compatible alternatives.

paragraphs: A flow-based generator can act as a prior when reconstructing an image from incomplete measurements. Optimizing only its initial noise requires differentiating through the entire generation trajectory, which consumes memory and can be unstable. MS-Flow instead distributes the optimization across intermediate latent states.

The trajectory is split into segments whose local dynamics are enforced separately. Matching penalties couple neighboring segments, and optimization alternates between updating latent states and satisfying the observed data. The method therefore treats the generative path as a structured object to adjust, rather than one long computation controlled solely at its starting point.

Experiments on inpainting, super-resolution, computed tomography, and other recovery tasks improve reconstruction quality while reducing memory consumption. The contribution is a trajectory-level optimization strategy that makes strong flow priors more practical for inverse problems. Local consistency and observation consistency work together to retain the generator’s structure while adapting its output to the available measurements.
icml-2026-trajectory-stitching-for-solvi.tldr: MS-Flow optimizes and stitches intermediate latent states to solve inverse problems with lower memory use and better reconstructions.

paragraphs: A few extreme weights or activations can stretch a quantizer’s range and damage low-bit language-model accuracy. Fixed transforms such as Hadamard rotations reduce this problem without adapting to the data. WUSH derives transforms specifically for joint weight-and-activation quantization under a standard block-quantization setup.

The construction combines a Hadamard backbone with a data-dependent second-moment component, producing a nonorthogonal transform. Closed-form analysis gives near-optimality for integer and floating-point quantizers under stated assumptions. An efficient fused GPU implementation makes the adaptive transform usable alongside low-precision matrix multiplication.

In four-bit weight and activation experiments, WUSH improves over strong Hadamard-based baselines. On one Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct configuration, gains are 2.8 average points with round-to-nearest quantization and 0.7 with GPTQ; per-layer throughput reaches 5.8 times BF16. The contribution connects quantizer-specific theory with a practical implementation rather than treating all rotations as equally appropriate.
icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.tldr: WUSH uses data-adaptive block transforms to improve four-bit LLM quantization while retaining efficient GPU execution.

paragraphs: Annealing methods search for good network configurations by controlling how freely units change, often through a temperature schedule chosen in advance. This paper replaces that global schedule with local decisions. Each unit determines its own temperature when it updates, based on how well nearby constraints are satisfied.

The resulting behavior lets poorly satisfied regions continue searching while already satisfactory regions remain stable. Search in a difficult region also continues as long as its constraints remain unsatisfied, rather than ending after a predetermined number of cycles. All processing occurs at the unit level, making the mechanism computationally simple.

The reported comparison finds global maxima more quickly and consistently than externally scheduled systems, including the referenced Boltzmann-machine approach. The contribution is a locally adaptive search process for constraint-satisfaction networks. Its central insight is that different parts of a network can need different amounts of continued exploration at the same moment.
neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.tldr: Automatic local annealing lets each unit adjust its own search temperature, keeping difficult regions active while stable regions settle.

paragraphs: The vestibulo-ocular reflex stabilizes retinal images by moving the eyes during rapid head motion. This paper uses that behavior to investigate a broader hypothesis: the cerebellum actively controls the acquisition of sensory information. The question is whether eye-movement control should change dynamically even within a head movement.

Viewing the system through statistical estimation theory leads the authors to argue that the reflex’s transfer function should be adjusted rapidly and continuously. That differs from treating it as a fixed or only slowly adaptable feature. They propose that the cerebellar cortex directly controls these changes.

The paper develops a testable physiological hypothesis and proposes experiments to assess it. Its significance is a shift from treating sensory input as something the nervous system simply receives to considering how motor control shapes the quality of that input. The theoretical proposal is not presented as an already confirmed experimental account of cerebellar function.
neurips-1988-neural-control-of-sensory-a.tldr: A statistical-estimation account proposes that the cerebellum rapidly adjusts the vestibulo-ocular reflex to improve sensory acquisition.

paragraphs: A neural classifier with high-dimensional inputs often requires many adjustable parameters and substantial hardware. With a fixed training corpus, that flexibility can exceed what the data support and weaken generalization. This paper studies ways to manage the connection between input size, model complexity, and available examples.

The authors discuss dimensionality reduction and prior knowledge in the context of isolated-word recognition. Reducing the representation’s dimensionality can lower the burden on the classifier, while prior structure can guide which distinctions it needs to represent. The application provides a concrete setting in which large input patterns must be classified from limited data.

The contribution is a treatment of representation and model design as part of the learning problem, rather than assuming that a larger network is always the right response to complex inputs. It highlights a practical constraint that links statistical and hardware efficiency: a compact, informed representation can make useful learning possible within both data and implementation limits.
neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.tldr: The paper examines dimensionality reduction and prior knowledge as ways to control network complexity in isolated-word recognition.

paragraphs: A trained neural system can encounter hardware faults after its weights have been learned. This paper examines that operational setting for Albus’ CMAC network, asking how its configuration affects sensitivity to damaged adjustable weights. The study distinguishes faults by what they do to the stored value.

For loss-of-weight faults, increasing the network’s generalization reduces sensitivity. For saturated-weight faults, the same change increases sensitivity. The two cases therefore reveal opposite responses to one design choice, rather than a single overall notion of fault tolerance.

The finding matters because a configuration that handles one failure mode well may be worse under another. Evaluating only an average or generic fault model could conceal that difference. The paper’s contribution is a fault-specific characterization of CMAC behavior after training, showing that robustness decisions need to reflect the kind of weight corruption expected during operation.
neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.tldr: Increasing CMAC generalization improves tolerance to lost weights but worsens sensitivity to saturated weights.

paragraphs: An arm must often control both where it moves and the forces it applies. Muscle redundancy complicates learning because several agonist–antagonist combinations can produce the same joint torque. This paper proposes a parallel-hierarchical neural controller that addresses trajectory and force learning together.

The model combines Hogan’s control method with feedback-error learning. Two hierarchical laws derived using the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse favor either small changes in muscle tension or small changes in motor commands. Those choices resolve ambiguity in the inverse model by specifying how the redundant control possibilities should be used.

Artificial-muscle-arm experiments and computer simulations demonstrate the approach. The contribution is a coordination of learning and control constraints: feedback errors train the model, while the hierarchical laws make the inverse problem better defined. This provides a practical route to simultaneous motion and force control rather than treating redundancy only as an obstacle to learning.
neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.tldr: A parallel-hierarchical controller combines feedback-error learning and redundancy-resolving control laws for joint trajectory and force control.

paragraphs: Speech production depends on how muscle commands move articulators, so a useful model needs to capture the musculoskeletal dynamics underlying sound production. This paper learns those forward dynamics from physiological measurements. It uses articulator motion and electromyography rather than relying only on acoustic observations.

A neural network maps motor commands and muscle activity to the resulting articulator behavior. After training, simulated perturbations probe properties of the learned system, including natural frequency, damping, and couplings between articulators. These tests examine whether the model captures meaningful dynamic relationships rather than merely reproducing recorded trajectories.

A cascade network then generates continuous motor commands from sequences of discrete articulatory targets. The contribution connects a learned physiological dynamics model with a mechanism for organizing movement commands over time. It offers a neural-network framework for studying both how speech movements unfold and how a sequence of intended articulations can be translated into continuous control.
neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.tldr: Physiological movement and EMG data train neural forward dynamics for speech, then support continuous commands from discrete articulatory targets.

paragraphs: Standard gradient-based training assumes enough smoothness to make derivatives useful, but neural transfer functions and losses can contain sharp corners. This paper addresses networks with piecewise-linear activations and nonsmooth error measures. It focuses on difficulties that arise when ordinary gradient methods are applied without accounting for those properties.

The authors draw on nonsmooth optimization to construct a learning algorithm appropriate to that setting. Their motivation includes an error measure based on the maximum norm, which they report can avoid difficulties encountered with the usual Euclidean-norm formulation. The optimization method must therefore handle the loss’s geometry rather than smooth it away implicitly.

The contribution expands the set of network and objective choices that can be trained with a principled algorithm. It emphasizes that changing an error measure can offer benefits only if the training procedure is compatible with the resulting mathematical structure. Nonsmoothness becomes a property to model explicitly, not merely an implementation inconvenience.
neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.tldr: A nonsmooth-optimization approach trains feedforward networks with piecewise-linear components and maximum-norm-based errors.

paragraphs: Neighboring image regions often share a coherent underlying property, such as surface depth. Earlier unsupervised learning exploited that coherence to discover depth and interpolate it from nearby values. This paper addresses the important exception: a depth discontinuity separates surfaces that should not be averaged together.

The authors propose two approaches. One detects discontinuity cases and rejects them from the ordinary interpolation procedure. The other learns a mixture of specialized interpolators, recognizing boundary locations and selecting asymmetric experts that use information from the appropriate side rather than crossing the boundary.

The contribution extends coherence-based learning to scenes whose structure is only piecewise smooth. A boundary changes which nearby observations are informative, so local prediction must depend on more than spatial proximity alone. The expert-based construction offers a way to retain useful interpolation within surfaces while avoiding the false continuity created by blending across separate objects.
neurips-1991-learning-to-make-coherent-p.tldr: Discontinuity-aware models detect surface boundaries and select asymmetric interpolators that preserve depth coherence without crossing edges.

paragraphs: An agent that learns several related tasks should be able to reuse earlier solutions when facing a longer task made from familiar parts. This paper studies composite Markovian decision tasks formed by concatenating simpler elemental tasks. The agent is not given the temporal boundaries between those parts.

A modular architecture and an incremental dynamic-programming algorithm learn both task solutions and a temporal decomposition of composite tasks. Training includes elemental and composite examples. This allows the system to discover where reusable subsolutions belong rather than requiring a manually specified sequence structure.

Under stated conditions, solving a composite task requires only inexpensive modifications to the solutions of its elements. The contribution provides a constructive account of transfer through temporal composition. It explains how learning a collection of simpler behaviors can reduce later computation when their structure is recognized and reused within a more complex decision problem.
neurips-1991-the-efficient-learning-of-m.tldr: A modular dynamic-programming learner discovers task decompositions and reuses elemental solutions to solve composite decision sequences efficiently.

paragraphs: The same continuous trajectory can be sampled or performed at different speeds, making a fixed temporal representation unreliable. Time Warping Invariant Neural Networks modify a recurrent architecture to remove that variation. The paper studies how continuous-time structure changes both invariance and memory of earlier inputs.

The analysis argues that TWINN can eliminate time warping in the considered formulation and retain longer input history than the compared neural-network finite automaton. The authors relate this memory property to difficulties encountered when training finite-automaton models on long strings. The architecture therefore addresses sequence representation as well as timing variability.

A trajectory-classification example combines variable sampling rates, internal state, continuous dynamics, and distorted paths. TWINN learns the task in 100 iterations, while the tested time-delay network fails. The contribution demonstrates how an architectural treatment of temporal continuity can handle a difficult timing-sensitive problem, with the comparative result tied to that constructed example.
neurips-1992-time-warping-invariant-neur.tldr: TWINN modifies recurrent processing to handle time-warped continuous trajectories and succeeds on a difficult trajectory-classification example.

paragraphs: Many language-processing tasks need a representation of word meaning that can be learned for a large vocabulary. This paper derives distributed semantic vectors from how words co-occur in a corpus. The approach uses contextual statistics rather than requiring a manually specified semantic description for every word.

A large-scale linear-regression method induces representations for 50,000 words. The learned vectors encode semantic information in a shared distributed space, allowing relationships among words to be expressed through their positions in that representation. The emphasis is on an efficient corpus-based construction that can operate at substantial vocabulary size.

The representations are successfully applied to word-sense disambiguation with a nearest-neighbor method. That application tests whether the induced space supports a concrete semantic decision rather than only descriptive similarity. The contribution links large-scale distributional learning with a simple downstream procedure, illustrating the usefulness of reusable word representations beyond the statistics used to create them.
neurips-1992-word-space-45e26192f3.tldr: Word Space learns distributed semantic vectors for 50,000 words from co-occurrence statistics and applies them to word-sense disambiguation.

paragraphs: Odor processing in bees involves interactions between the antennal lobe and the mushroom bodies. This paper asks how higher-level input might influence the feature extraction occurring in the antennal lobe. It uses anatomical structure to investigate feedback between processing stages rather than treating sensory processing as purely feedforward.

The model combines simplified neurons with an architecture grounded in detailed anatomical observations. Within that structure, the authors examine mechanisms of modulation and control between glomeruli and mushroom bodies. Their preliminary conclusion is that central input is needed to fine-tune the antennal lobe’s representation.

The proposed feedback helps transform diffuse glomerular activity into more focused odor representations during presentation. The contribution is a biologically structured computational hypothesis about the role of top-down signals in sensory refinement. Its preliminary status matters: the model suggests a mechanism for sharpening odor information, rather than establishing that the simulated feedback is the only biological route to that effect.
neurips-1993-odor-processing-in-the-bee-.tldr: An anatomically grounded bee-olfaction model proposes that mushroom-body feedback sharpens antennal-lobe odor representations.

paragraphs: A binary observation may reflect several hidden factors at once, whereas a standard mixture model assigns it to one component. This paper develops an unsupervised model in which multiple hidden causes jointly explain different subsets of observed dimensions. The key challenge is how their contributions should combine.

The authors examine the mixing function that turns beliefs about several cluster centers into a reconstruction. They identify a weakness in the common weighted-sum-plus-sigmoid construction and propose a different nonlinearity. Reconstruction errors guide both recognition of active causes and learning of the representations themselves.

Experiments recover coherent multiple-cause structure from noisy test data and printed-character images. The contribution is a representation that can compose latent explanations instead of forcing each example into a single exclusive cluster. Here hidden causes are components of a generative model; the empirical recovery does not automatically establish real-world causal identification from observational data.
neurips-1993-unsupervised-learning-of-mi.tldr: A revised nonlinear mixing rule lets an unsupervised binary-data model discover compositional hidden factors rather than exclusive clusters.

paragraphs: Worst-case complexity measures can make generalization bounds pessimistic when the training distribution and target restrict which label patterns actually arise. This paper studies consistent learning under additional conditions on those ingredients and the hypothesis class. It seeks a sample requirement that reflects the relevant problem rather than the hardest possible configuration.

The analysis links sample complexity to an average number of implementable dichotomies on sampled data. This replaces reliance on the largest shattered set, which defines VC dimension. The distinction allows the theory to account for distributional structure that a worst-case combinatorial measure can ignore.

The resulting upper bounds improve substantially and can be below VC dimension or even finite when VC dimension is infinite. Those conclusions do not contradict ordinary worst-case theory, because the model adds restrictions on the learning setting. The contribution shows how distribution-sensitive counting can yield more informative guarantees about the data needed for accurate, confident learning.
neurips-1994-generalisation-in-feedforwa.tldr: Distribution-sensitive counting of label patterns yields sharper sample-complexity bounds than worst-case VC dimension in the restricted setting.

paragraphs: In many classification tasks, collecting inputs is inexpensive while obtaining their labels is costly. A supervised learner may therefore have access to far more raw examples than labeled ones. This paper proposes using the distributional information in those unlabeled inputs to strengthen supervised training.

The method augments the information supplied by labeled examples with structure learned from the unlabeled sample distribution. Its purpose is to make better use of the examples already available, rather than treating every unannotated observation as unusable. The learning setup remains directed toward a classification task defined by the labeled data.

Empirical tests show significant accuracy improvements when the supervised learner is well below its asymptotic accuracy level. That condition highlights where additional distributional information can be especially valuable: the labeled sample alone has not yet exhausted the model’s achievable performance. The contribution is an early demonstration that useful supervision can be supplemented by abundant unlabeled data.
neurips-1995-using-unlabeled-data-for-su.tldr: Using unlabeled input-distribution information improves supervised classification when labeled-data performance remains below its asymptotic level.

paragraphs: How many hidden layers are needed to represent a function depends on more than parameter count. This paper studies threshold-unit networks for binary functions, concentrating on the geometry of two-dimensional decision regions. It extends an earlier characterization that excluded multiple boundary intersections and restricted attention to compact domains.

The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for one-hidden-layer representation near multiple intersection points and near infinity. These local results fill gaps in the earlier setting. They then ask whether satisfying all such local requirements is enough to guarantee a single hidden layer can represent the whole function.

It is not: a nonlocal configuration called a critical cycle prevents global representation despite the added local conditions. The contribution identifies a genuinely global obstacle to shallow-network expressivity. This shows why checking neighborhoods separately can miss dependencies among decision boundaries that determine whether an additional hidden layer is required.
neurips-1996-multilayer-neural-networks-.tldr: A critical-cycle obstruction shows that locally compatible threshold decision regions can still require more than one hidden layer globally.
